answer: A guild hall with an ivory tower keeps its roster honest by demanding a widening ring of sponsors. The first applicant needs 1 established member to sponsor it, the tenth needs 10, and the twentieth needs 20, each sponsor giving up a single slot that cannot be spent twice in one epoch. A farmer of fake names meets a cost that climbs in a widening spiral with every addition: 20 fakes require 210 different sponsors, and a handful of allies cannot lend the same plume of credibility to twenty strangers at once. Each new name must earn fresh backing from people outside its own circle.
